name: Target 2013 Data Breach
description: MITRE ATT&CK mapping of the 2013 Target payment card breach. Green = high confidence, amber = medium, red = low/possible. Verify against the Senate Commerce 'Kill Chain' report.

techniques.comment: HIGH. Attackers used BlackPOS (Kaptoxa), commercially sold POS malware, rather than building their own.
MEDIUM. Fazio Mechanical (HVAC vendor) was reportedly compromised via a phishing email. Reported, not officially confirmed.
MEDIUM. Malware on the vendor's systems reportedly captured login credentials.
MEDIUM. Possible theft of stored credentials from the vendor's systems.
HIGH. Access came through Fazio's trusted vendor relationship with Target.
HIGH. Stolen vendor credentials were used to log into Target's vendor portal. Internal account reuse for movement is medium confidence.
HIGH. Legitimate credentials made the access look like normal vendor activity.
LOW / POSSIBLE. Sources are unclear how attackers moved from the vendor portal into the internal network. A web application flaw is one theory.
LOW to MEDIUM. Attackers reportedly obtained internal/Active Directory credentials to expand access.
HIGH. Weak network segmentation let attackers move from the vendor-facing network toward internal servers and POS systems.
LOW to MEDIUM. Malware reportedly pushed to POS terminals via internal deployment tooling.
LOW to MEDIUM. Same as above, in the Execution tactic.
LOW to MEDIUM. Malware and tools reportedly disguised as legitimate software.
HIGH. BlackPOS scraped card data from POS RAM during transactions. ATT&CK has no dedicated RAM-scraping technique, so this is the closest fit.
HIGH. Stolen data was staged on compromised internal servers before exfiltration.
HIGH. Data was sent out over FTP to external servers.
